narrative.overview: The system takes its world from Vietnamese cement tile (gạch bông). The ground is a cool cement grey, the navigation rail is a deep peacock teal, and every department owns one geometric tile pattern drawn from plain CSS gradients. Workload is shown as tiles laid in rows, not as bars or charts. It is a working queue tool: dense, quiet, hairline-ruled, with tabular numerals, and it refuses the grey-screen-with-one-accent SaaS default.
keyCharacteristics: Cement-grey canvas with near-white surface panels separated by hairline rules, not shadows.
Deep teal rail at the left on desktop, collapsing to a top band on mobile.
Eight department tile patterns used as swatches, a border band, and workload squares.
Status is a tinted chip or a coloured ring; priority is an outline; "mine" is purple.
No icons or glyphs anywhere; meaning is carried by words, pattern, and colour.

rules.name: The Reserved Purple Rule
rules.body: Purple appears only to say "this waits on you". It never decorates, never marks a status, and never appears on a department.

rules.name: The Status Is Not Priority Rule
rules.body: Status is a tinted fill chip; priority is an outline ring (1px neutral for low and medium, 2px ochre for high, 2px brick for urgent). The two must never both read as fills.

rules.name: The Small And Plain Rule
rules.body: Text is 0.75rem or 0.875rem for almost everything. Size jumps are reserved for page titles. Do not set uppercase, letter-spaced label text above headings.

rules.name: The Hairline Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate regions with a 1px line or a tonal step. Shadows are not part of the built system.

dos: Do write the department name beside any tile swatch; the tile is a mark, not a label.
Do keep status as tinted chips and priority as outline rings.
Do reserve purple (mine-600 family) for work waiting on the viewer, at badge, row-tint, and nav-count level only.
Do use hairline borders and tonal steps to separate regions.
Do keep numerals tabular and text at 0.75rem or 0.875rem except page titles.
Do label mock data as replaceable wherever it is shown (the viewer switcher carries the sample-data note).
Do build any new pattern from plain CSS gradients on a flat ground and ink pair.
donts: Don't use icons, glyphs, or emoji; meaning is words, pattern, and colour.
Don't introduce a ninth hue or reuse purple for anything but "waiting on me".
Don't use a pale single-accent grey SaaS layout, gradient text, or heavy drop shadows.
Don't use circles or pills for workload marks; tiles are squares with small corners.
Don't colour a department by status or a status by department; pattern says department, ring or chip says status.
